gap: BHD PASSES the mandatory gate: 0 differing pixels out of 16,876,800 sampled, in a same-session same-data A/B under data-product=bhd-erp with the wave sheet toggled off vs on across dashboard, /customer, /invoice at 1440x900 and dashboard at 390x844. The stale baseline-*.png files differ (2,438,500 / 307,861 / 953,283 / 596,967 px) but that is data drift, proven because the diff is BYTE-IDENTICAL with the wave sheet fully disabled (307,861 and 953,283 unchanged to the pixel). The rail logo reading BHD is also a capture artifact, NavigationContainer picks the P&P mark off the hostname, not off data-product. So the verdict is design, and it is the rail's active state. On /customer the SATURATED treatment (.ant-menu-submenu-title, background rgb(43,87,216) solid, icon rgb(255,255,255)) sits on FAVORITES, which is merely an open submenu, while the page you are actually on, Customers, gets rgba(43,87,216,0.11) with a GREY rgb(91,103,121) icon. Two competing 'you are here' languages on screen at once and the loud one is on the wrong item, with the current page's icon not even carrying the accent. The bar has exactly one: a pale-blue rounded square with a BLUE icon, on the current page. appshell-r2 named this four rounds ago. Around it: 17 label-less top-level rail items of which Reports alone is an in a different icon language and colour from the other 16; a topbar right cluster of 8 controls in 4 idioms (search field with two hint chips, three grey outline icons including a persistent muted-speaker-with-x, the word 'English' as text among icons, a globe, a bell with a red '15', a filled avatar) against Wave's wordmark plus one gift icon; and a 56x56 fixed FAB, inline-styled so no stylesheet can reach it, carrying a slate gradient and an off-palette rgba(0,115,230,0.4) glow over every page at both viewports. The list-page table and the #f5f9ff content frame ARE bar-grade, and the Plus Jakarta Sans headings get the bar's hardest call right. The frame is not the problem; the furniture in it is. (The beach orb bottom-right is TanStack devtools behind import.meta.env.DEV at RootApp.jsx:457, discounted.)
